finding.claim: /invoice/<inv_id> has no authentication or ownership check, so any unauthenticated caller can read any invoice by ID (IDOR / broken access control).
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP GET with attacker-chosen inv_id in the URL path.
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returning the full invoice record from INVOICES (invoices.py:10).

trace.note: inv_id taken from URL path with no auth decorator or hook.
INVOICES.get(inv_id) or abort(404); only handles missing IDs.
Full record returned to caller without checking g.user or customer ownership.

finding.guards_checked: No before_request hook, decorator, or g.user check in this file. The 404 on line 9 only handles missing IDs. The sibling /my/invoice route does enforce ownership, so this route is inconsistent with the rest of the app.

verdict.guard_found: none. invoices.py:8-10 has no decorator, before_request hook, or g.user check. The only guard is abort(404) at invoices.py:9, which handles missing IDs only. The sibling route at invoices.py:16-17 does perform an ownership check, so the omission is specific to this route. The directory contains no other .py files (Glob returned only invoices.py), so no app-level hook is visible.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: the route at invoices.py:7-10 takes inv_id from the path, returns INVOICES[inv_id] via jsonify with no auth or ownership check, and an anonymous caller can reach it; the only caveat is that g.user is referenced at invoices.py:16 and 23, so an auth hook registered outside this directory could exist, which I cannot see.

finding.claim: /my/* routes depend on g.user set by unseen upstream code and do not reject unauthenticated requests; with g.user unset they fail with a 500 instead of 401/403.
finding.source: Request with no authenticated user, so g.user is never set.
finding.sink: g.user["id"] access in the ownership check (invoices.py:16) and in list_mine (invoices.py:23).

trace.note: get_my_invoice entry point; no auth check.
g.user["id"] raises AttributeError if g.user is unset, producing a 500.
list_mine entry point; same g.user dependency at line 23.

finding.guards_checked: The ownership comparison (!=) is correct and returns 404 for both missing and foreign invoices, so there is no existence oracle. Security relies entirely on authentication code that is not in this file.

verdict.guard_found: none. invoices.py:15 (abort(404) on a missing invoice) runs before the g.user access at :16, and no auth check, before_request hook, or g.user setter exists in the repo (only invoices.py is present). The ownership check at :16-17 is never reached when g.user is unset.
verdict.reason: Trace is accurate: invoices.py:16 and :23 read g.user["id"] with no guard, so an anonymous request gets a 500 (AttributeError) at :16 for any existing invoice ID, while a missing ID returns 404 at :15. The candidate's guards_checked says there is no existence oracle, which is wrong for anonymous callers, since the 404/500 difference reveals whether an invoice ID exists. Severity is low (error-handling defect plus an ID-existence oracle, not a data disclosure), and whether the app rejects anonymous requests upstream is out of this repo's scope.

finding.claim: One invoice record without a 'customer' key makes /my/invoices fail for every customer, not just the owner of that record (logic flaw / DoS).
finding.source: A record in INVOICES lacking the 'customer' key, e.g. from a partial write elsewhere.
finding.sink: i["customer"] in the list comprehension (invoices.py:23) raises KeyError and fails the whole response.

trace.note: Iterates INVOICES.values(); i["customer"] raises KeyError on the malformed record, returning 500 for all callers.

finding.guards_checked: No .get() or schema validation on the record. Single-record failure is not isolated.

verdict.guard_found: none. invoices.py:23 has no .get() or schema check, but no attacker-controlled input reaches the malformed-record condition. The only INVOICES writes in the directory are its initialization at invoices.py:4. The record writer the candidate cites ("partial write elsewhere") is not in the code available.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (invoices.py:22-23 does iterate INVOICES.values() and index i["customer"] unguarded), but the attacker cannot place a record lacking 'customer' into INVOICES: the only data source in this code is the empty dict at invoices.py:4 and no writer exists here, so the KeyError requires data corruption outside any attacker's reach, not an attacker-triggerable DoS.

finding.claim: Ownership check may be bypassed by a null match if g.user['id'] is None or otherwise equal to an invoice's customer value (conditional on upstream auth behaviour).
finding.source: A g.user object whose id is None or matches a record's customer value, produced by unseen auth code.
finding.sink: The != comparison at invoices.py:16 allowing the protected jsonify(inv) at line 18 to run.

trace.note: inv loaded from INVOICES by attacker-chosen inv_id.
inv["customer"] != g.user["id"] passes when both values are equal, including both None.

finding.guards_checked: No check in this file rejects None or missing user IDs. Only exploitable if upstream auth can yield such a user and some invoices have a matching customer value; not confirmable from this file.

verdict.guard_found: none in invoices.py: no before_request/auth decorator on get_my_invoice (invoices.py:13-14), and the only check is the != comparison at invoices.py:16, which aborts on mismatch and proceeds on equality as the trace says. The directory contains only invoices.py, so the code that sets g.user (the auth code) cannot be read.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (invoices.py:15 loads inv, :16 proceeds when inv["customer"] equals g.user["id"], :18 returns it), but whether g.user["id"] can be None or equal a stored customer value depends on auth code that is not in the directory, so the exploitability cannot be decided here.

finding.claim: Full invoice record is returned with no field allowlist, which may expose internal fields to customers (informational, conditional on record contents).
finding.source: Any caller of /invoice/<inv_id> (F1) or an authenticated caller of /my/invoice/<inv_id>.
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) at invoices.py:10 and invoices.py:18 serializing the entire stored dict.

trace.note: Entire INVOICES entry serialized to the response.
Same unfiltered serialization on the customer-facing route.

finding.guards_checked: No field filtering or serializer in this file. Impact depends on whether stored records contain internal-only fields, which cannot be seen here.

verdict.guard_found: none. There is no field filter or serializer in invoices.py. Line 10 (`return jsonify(inv)`) and line 18 (`return jsonify(inv)`) serialize the whole stored dict, as the candidate says. The only checks are the 404 abort on a missing ID (line 9) and the ownership comparison on line 16, which applies only to the /my/ route.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (invoices.py:10 and :18 serialize the whole `inv` dict with no filtering), but whether this leaks anything depends on what fields INVOICES records hold, and `INVOICES = {}` at line 4 is empty and populated nowhere in this file, so an exposure of internal fields cannot be confirmed from the code available.
